definition.name: pretty_good_measurement
definition.definition: A pretty good measurement (PGM), also called the square-root measurement or least-squares measurement, is a POVM for quantum state discrimination. Given a set of states {rho_i} with prior probabilities {p_i}, the PGM operators are M_i = p_i * Gamma^{-1/2} rho_i Gamma^{-1/2}, where Gamma = sum_i p_i rho_i is the average state. The PGM achieves success probability P_PGM >= P_OPT^2 (Barnum-Knill bound [BK02]), making it near-optimal. In this paper, Mix(GPS) is shown to implement the PGM over the rank-r Hilbert-Schmidt measure (Proposition A.1).
